abstract: The cerebral cortex consists of immense numbers of diverse cell types derived from radial glial progenitor (RGP) cells. How RGPs generate appropriate quantities of distinct cell types to safeguard a brain of correct size is not well understood. However, genetic aberrations in human, including mutations in PTEN, lead to cortical malformation such as macrocephaly, albeit with unknown etiology. Here, we used mosaic analysis with double markers (MADM)-based clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping to decipher the role of Pten in RGP lineage progression during cortical ontogeny. Although neurogenic RGP lineage progression was altered and projection neuron production doubled in the absence of Pten, cortical astrogenesis was drastically increased. Through epistasis experiments, we show that the loss of Pten uncouples astrogenesis from essential growth factor signaling hubs, funneling into MAPK (mitogen-activated protein kinase). Collectively, our results suggest that Pten regulates RGP lineage progression with distinct sequential functions in corticogenesis to safeguard the emergence of a correctly sized cortex.

summary: MADM clonal analysis and single-cell phenotyping show Pten controls radial glia lineage progression and astrocyte production via Mapk1/3 signaling in neocortex.
title: Pten regulates neurogenic radial glia lineage progression and tunes neocortical astrocyte production in Mapk1/3-dependent pathway.
